findings.title: Operator docs say the Operator "will fail" without `rolling-updates`, but no operator code checks the feature
findings.description:
The new CAUTION block states that the feature must be enabled or "the {project_name} Operator will fail". Nothing under `operator/src/main` references `rolling-updates`, `ROLLING_UPDATES` or `update-compatibility`. `UpgradeLogicFactory#create` (`operator/src/main/java/org/keycloak/operator/upgrade/UpgradeLogicFactory.java:35-43`) chooses the logic purely from `spec.update.strategy`, and neither upgrade logic calls the gated CLI commands.

The updated test contradicts the docs too. In `UpgradeTest.java:105-107`, `createInitialDeployment` returns early for the `null` strategy without enabling the feature, and those cases are still expected to succeed. The YAML example at lines 475-479 nonetheless shows the feature as required for both `Recreate` and `<not set>`.

Either the operator should validate the feature when `spec.update` is used, or the caution should be dropped or reworded.

findings.title: New exit-code contract is not asserted, and the `check` gate has no test
findings.description:
The guide tells consumers to rely only on the exit code of `check`, and this change alters two codes: `RECREATE_UPGRADE_EXIT_CODE` goes from 4 to 3, and `FEATURE_DISABLED = 4` is new. The tests do not pin either:
- **Feature disabled:** `testFeatureNotEnabled` asserts only the error text, not exit code 4, and covers only `metadata`. The identical gate in `UpdateCompatibilityCheck.run()` (lines 46-50) is never exercised.
- **Recreate:** `testWrongVersions` (lines 86-107) asserts only the message, so the 4-to-3 change would pass unnoticed if reverted.

Add `assertEquals(CompatibilityResult.FEATURE_DISABLED, result.exitCode())` for both subcommands and `assertEquals(CompatibilityResult.RECREATE_UPGRADE_EXIT_CODE, result.exitCode())` in `testWrongVersions`.

findings.title: Feature-gate block is duplicated in both subcommands
findings.description: The same five-line guard appears in `UpdateCompatibilityMetadata.java:46-50`. Both classes extend `AbstractUpdatesCommand`, which already implements `Runnable` and owns `printFeatureDisabled()`. A final `run()` in the base class that performs the gate, preview warning and `validateConfig()` before delegating to an abstract hook would stop a future subcommand from forgetting the gate.

findings.title: `FEATURE_DISABLED` breaks the sibling naming pattern, and the feature key is hardcoded
findings.description: The neighbouring constants are `ROLLING_UPGRADE_EXIT_CODE` and `RECREATE_UPGRADE_EXIT_CODE`; the new one lacks the `_EXIT_CODE` suffix. Separately, `AbstractUpdatesCommand.java:84` hardcodes `'rolling-updates'` in the message instead of using `Profile.Feature.ROLLING_UPDATES.getKey()`, as `EventPropertyMappers.java:22` does for its feature.

findings.title: Exit code 4 is reused with a different meaning
findings.description: Code 4 previously meant "recreate required" and now means "feature disabled". Moving recreate to 3 is right: `update-compatibility.adoc:128-130` already documented 3, and it avoids picocli's reserved 1 and 2. The command is preview, so this is acceptable, but any script written against the old binary will silently treat "feature disabled" as "recreate". A line in the release or migration notes would help. The new doc row for code 4 (`update-compatibility.adoc:132-134`) says "Rolling Upgrade is not possible", yet `metadata` also returns 4, where that wording does not apply.

findings.title: `UpgradeTest` enables the feature only for an explicit strategy and overwrites existing enabled features
findings.description: The `null`-strategy cases never set the feature and rely on `operator/scripts/Dockerfile-custom-image:5` baking in `--features=rolling-updates` when a custom image is used; that coupling is not commented anywhere. `setEnabledFeatures(List.of(...))` at line 115 also replaces any features already on the spec rather than appending. That is harmless with today's default test CR but fragile.

findings.title: Feature gate runs after the profile is initialised and stops execution correctly
findings.description: `Profile.isFeatureEnabled` dereferences `Profile.getInstance()` (`Profile.java:408-410`), which would throw if the profile were unset. It is set: `Picocli.parseAndRun` calls `PropertyMappers.sanitizeDisabledMappers()` at `Picocli.java:128` before `cmd.execute`, and that calls `Environment.getCurrentOrCreateFeatureProfile()` (`PropertyMappers.java:302-306`). The explicit `return` after `picocli.exit(...)` is needed because `Picocli.exit` (`Picocli.java:203-208`) does not terminate in test launch mode. `--features` is accepted by these commands because `getIncludeOptions` (`Picocli.java:674-675`) includes build-time options when `--optimized` is absent.

findings.title: `ROLLING_UPDATES` feature declaration follows the enum's conventions
findings.description: A `Type.PREVIEW`, version-1 feature yields the key `rolling-updates`, matching the docs, Dockerfile and tests. `FeaturesDistTest.java:32-33` builds its expected preview list from `Feature.values()`, and the help approval files render feature values as `<...>`, so no snapshot needs updating.
